content:
If President Don really wanted to see Kaitlan Collins' delight, he should have tuned into CNN last night.

The president's favorite journalist couldn't stop laughing while anchoring "The Source" last night, as she reported on the embarrassing moment Republican Missouri Senator Eric Schmitt revealed during former Special Counsel Jack Smith's testimony the day before. Collins found hilarious Republican Alabama Senator Katie Britt's real-time reaction to the hearing, and ultimately summed up the disaster in one line.

Chuckling, Collins said: "This is absolutely one of the most classic moments in the history of Capitol Hill hearings."

During the hearing, Schmitt asked Smith: "Did you attend the NBA game between the Golden State Warriors and the Atlanta Hawks on February 3, 2024?"

After Smith said blankly that he had not, Schmitt began explaining his question, saying the game was held in Atlanta—the same day Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis admitted to an extramarital affair with another prosecutor, Nathan Wade. At the time, Willis, like Smith, was busy prosecuting Donald Trump over his 2020 election interference.

Schmitt also produced what he thought was evidence—a screenshot he showed the committee of a text-message exchange allegedly involving Smith's staff, in which one message mentioned going to a "Hawks" game that day.

But what Schmitt thought would be a knockout blow ended up looking like an own goal. After a few rounds of back-and-forth, Smith finally recalled that he did indeed attend a Hawks game that day—but it wasn't in Atlanta… and it wasn't even an NBA game.

What he had actually gone to was an Iowa Hawkeyes game held in Maryland, specifically to watch current WNBA rookie sensation Caitlin Clark, then representing the University of Iowa, take on the University of Maryland in a women's college basketball matchup.

Progressive outlet MeidasTouch located and released footage of Smith at the Iowa-Maryland game on February 3, and HuffPost subsequently confirmed through a spokesperson for Smith that the person in the clip was indeed him.

After playing several clips on her CNN show of Schmitt confusing the Atlanta Hawks with the Iowa Hawkeyes, Collins—struggling to contain her laughter—asked one of her guests, Democratic strategist Paul Begala, for his take on the spectacle.

Begala said sarcastically: "Oh, poor Senator Schmitt." Then, with even more biting irony: "I'm glad they asked that question, okay? Because now everyone can see how smart Senator Schmitt is."

He added: "It really is unbelievably stupid. I have to say that. And holding this hearing in the first place is unbelievably stupid. There are still 35 days until the election, gas is $4.50 a gallon, diesel is $6.50 a gallon, beef is $6.92 a pound.... If you thought voters already wanted a change and were fed up with the Republicans before the hearing, they'll be even more fed up after it."

Collins's other guest, Republican strategist Shermichael Singleton, agreed with that view, stressing that the GOP must focus on affordability issues ahead of the November midterms.

When Collins asked Singleton whether Republicans should have invited Smith to testify before Congress, Singleton responded with visible exasperation: "For what?! What on earth did we get out of putting on this circus show?!"
